A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AffordDP and contain complete, readable main texts and appendices A–E. Their equations, figures, tables, and experiments can be matched despite notation changes and table reordering.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulation and real-world manipulation results, component ablations, and additional spatial-generalization and semantic-correspondence analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental outcomes, including success-rate tables and supplementary analyses.

M1.justification: The stated diffusion sampler is revised: Eq. 6 replaces the final predicted-noise term with random noise, and Eq. 7 removes the eta multiplier. Affordance transfer, encoders, conditioning, and adaptive guidance remain intact. These are limited specification changes; the PDFs do not establish an implementation change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same simulated OpenDoor and PullDrawer tasks and real-world OpenDoor, PullDrawer, and Pick&Place tasks. Seen instances, unseen instances/categories, spatial variation, and supplementary kitchen scenes are retained. The new limitations examples are not evaluated tasks.

E2.justification: DP and DP3 remain the evaluated policy baselines. Appendix D.3 and Figure 9 retain CLIP, DINOv2, SD, and SD-DINOv2 for semantic correspondence. Newly cited methods, including G3Flow, are not added to the experimental comparisons.

E3.justification: The object-specific and unified training protocols, demonstration counts, difficulty settings, success criteria, and experimental hyperparameters are unchanged. Both retain the 1,000-position spatial evaluation and the same real-world trial procedures.

E4.justification: Table 5 retains the same trajectory and affordance-guidance ablations. The variance-level experiments and supplementary spatial-generalization, semantic-correspondence, and unseen-kitchen analyses also remain unchanged.

E5.justification: The three-trial qualitative comparison and ten-trial per-object results retain their reporting practices. Neither version adds seed information, uncertainty intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: v1 Tables 1–3 correspond to v2 Tables 2, 3, and 1 with unchanged outcomes. Tables 4, 5, and 9 also retain their values. Appendix D still reports 65 DP3 successes versus 170 AffordDP successes across 1,000 spatial trials, and the qualitative findings are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 6–7 revise the denoising mathematics by distinguishing random noise from the network prediction and removing eta from the noise-scale expression. These exceed equivalent notation changes. The remaining mathematical development is retained, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims: transferable static and dynamic affordances and adaptive guidance improve diffusion-policy generalization to unseen instances and categories. Their scientific scope is unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix E replaces the specific multi-part ambiguity and long-horizon limitations with severe occlusion, visual distortion, and precise force-control limitations, illustrated by handling eggs. The conclusion retains its broader spatial-understanding and affordance-extraction caveats; result interpretations otherwise remain stable.

D1.justification: Appendices B–C and Table 8 retain the same collection, calibration, preprocessing, architecture, training, and inference details, including 4,096 points and the A100 40GB training disclosure. Project access information is unchanged. Naming gamma as a guidance weight explains an existing equation rather than disclosing a new implementation setting.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to G3Flow, Lift3D, spatial-temporal graph diffusion policy, MoManipVLA, and SeqAfford. Section 2.1 extends the existing comparison with GenDP to include G3Flow. This updates the literature coverage without substantially changing the research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 standardizes the DP abbreviation, changes affordance notation from A to Phi, explains noise and guidance symbols, updates author annotations, and adds acknowledgements. Appendix E is rewritten, but the overall narrative and section organization remain substantially the same.

P2.justification: Figures 2–3 correct input and trajectory labels and update notation. The three tables on page 7 change column placement and numbering, with minor caption, spacing, and supplementary-header adjustments elsewhere. The same figures and tables remain; no new result display is introduced.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves technical clarity by separating random noise from predicted noise in Eq. 6, explaining the guidance weight, and correcting diagram labels. Related-work coverage is also updated while empirical evidence remains unchanged. The limitations rewrite adds concrete occlusion and force-control caveats but drops the explicit long-horizon warning, limiting the net benefit.
